deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page is working material for Riemann's 1861 memoir 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides'. The ellipsoid has semi-axes a,b,c and uniform density ε (gravitational constant absorbed). Each paired quantity measures one component, about a principal axis, of the rotation and of the internal (vorticity) motion: g,g' for the a-axis (paired with b∓c), h,h' for the b-axis (paired with c∓a), k,k' for the c-axis (paired with a∓b). The potential integrals use Δ = sqrt((1+s/a²)(1+s/b²)(1+s/c²)), with s from 0 to ∞. σ is a pressure/normalisation constant; it is written δ on the next page.

Step 1. Two of the six evolution equations (listed in full on the next page):
0 = (a−b) dk/dt + 2 d(a−b)/dt·k + gh(a+b−2c)/2 + g'h'(a+b+2c)/2,
0 = (a+b) dk'/dt + 2 d(a+b)/dt·k' + gh'(a−b+2c)/2 + g'h(a−b−2c)/2.

Step 2. Riemann seeks stationary figures with k = k' = 0, so rotation and vorticity lie in the (a,b) principal plane.
- The h- and g-equations are then satisfied identically.
- The two equations above become gh(a+b−2c) + g'h'(a+b+2c) = 0 and gh'(a−b+2c) + g'h(a−b−2c) = 0.
- He solves them by setting
  h²/((a+b+2c)(a−b+2c)) = h'²/((a+b−2c)(a−b−2c)) = τ,
  g²/((a+b+2c)(b−a+2c)) = g'²/((a+b−2c)(b−a−2c)) = ρ.
- Explicitly (lower part of the page): h = sqrt(τ(2c+a+b)(2c+a−b)), h' = ±sqrt(τ(2c−a−b)(2c+b−a)), g = sqrt(ρ(2c+a+b)(2c+b−a)), g' = ±sqrt(ρ(2c−a−b)(2c+a−b)).
- With matching signs both equations vanish identically (my check).
- Reality of h,h',g,g' gives two admissible regimes:
  1) 2c > a+b, with τ > 0 and ρ > 0;
  2) 2c < a−b (so a > b), with τ > 0 and ρ < 0.
- This is the 'Summe/Differenz' condition of Riemann's published treatment of motions whose axes lie in a principal plane.

Step 3. Equilibrium (diagonal) equations.
- Kinetic coefficient along the a-axis: −(τ/2)[(a−c)((a+2c)²−b²) + (a+c)((a−2c)²−b²)] = −τ a(a²−b²). This uses (a−c)(a+2c)² = a³+3a²c−4c³.
- Along the c-axis: −(τ/2)[(c−a)((a+2c)²−b²) + (a+c)((a−2c)²−b²)] = τ c(3a²−4c²+b²).
- Equating to the gravitational terms gives
  (1) τa²(a²−b²) = 2επ∫a² ds/(Δ(a²+s)) − 2σ,
  (2) ρb²(b²−a²) = 2επ∫b² ds/(Δ(b²+s)) − 2σ,
  (3) −c²[τ(3a²−4c²+b²) + ρ(3b²−4c²+a²)] = 2επ∫c² ds/(Δ(c²+s)) − 2σ.

Step 4. Elimination. Put q = τ+ρ and p = a²τ + b²ρ.
- Since τ(3a²−4c²+b²) + ρ(3b²−4c²+a²) = 2p + (a²+b²−4c²)q, equation (3) becomes 2p + (a²+b²−4c²)q − 2σ/c² = −2επ∫ds/(Δ(c²+s)).
- (1) − (2) gives p(a²−b²) = 2επ∫(a²−b²)s ds/(Δ(a²+s)(b²+s)), by partial fractions.
- (1)/a² − (2)/b² gives q(a²−b²) = 2επ∫(b²−a²)ds/(Δ(a²+s)(b²+s)) + 2σ(a²−b²)/(a²b²).
- Substituting into (3) gives a linear equation for σ, whose coefficient is 1/c² + (4c²−a²−b²)/(a²b²) = (4c⁴−(a²+b²)c²+a²b²)/(a²b²c²). Hence the factor (4c⁴−(a²+b²)c²+a²b²)·2σ.

Step 5. Final result after eliminating σ (after one intermediate attempt):
- τ(a²−b²)(4c⁴−(a²+b²)c²+a²b²) = 2επ(c²−b²)∫ s ds/(Δ(b²+s)) · [(4c²+b²−a²)/(a²+s) − b²/(c²+s)].
- ρ(b²−a²)(same factor) = 2επ(c²−a²)∫ s ds/(Δ(a²+s)) · [(4c²+a²−b²)/(b²+s) − a²/(c²+s)].
- I verified the τ-formula by reducing everything to A=∫ds/(Δ(a²+s)), B, C. The coefficients of A, B and C agree identically. The ρ-formula follows by a↔b.

Step 6. Side cases.
(i) c = ∞ (elliptic-cylinder limit):
- The σ-equation reduces to 2σ/(a²b²) = 2επ∫ds/(Δ(a²+s)(b²+s)).
- Then τa²(a²−b²) = 2επ∫a² s ds/(Δ(a²+s)(b²+s)). I checked this.
(ii) Regime 1 with c = a:
- Equations (1) and (3) have equal right-hand sides.
- So −a²(b²−a²)(τ+3ρ) = τa²(a²−b²), hence ρ = 0. The motion degenerates to one with g = g' = 0, i.e. rotation/vorticity about the b-axis only.
(iii) Boundary of regime 2: 2c = a−b, written as 4c² = a²+b²−2ab, together with the limits c = 0 and b = 0.
(iv) Locating ρ = 0 in general:
- Riemann compares ∫ds/(Δ(1+s/a²)(1+s/c²)) with ∫ds/(Δ(1+s/b²)).
- Their difference is written as ∫ ds/Δ³ [s(1/a²+1/c²−1/b²) + s²/(a²c²)]. This is correct, since Δ² is the product of the three factors.
- The bottom-right scratch is algebra comparing the expressions a²+c²−a²c²/b², (c²−b²)/(4c²−b²), a²(2c²−b²)² etc. It appears aimed at the sign or location of the ρ = 0 boundary. Its purpose is not fully recoverable.
errors: The lower-page formula for g' reads ±sqrt(ρ(2c−a−b)(2c+b−a)), as far as legible. The definition g'² = ρ(a+b−2c)(b−a−2c) requires ρ(2c−a−b)(2c+a−b), which is also what makes the stationarity equations vanish. This is a slip, unless it is a misreading.

The first elimination attempt for τ is incomplete and partly inconsistent: τa²(a²−b²)(4c⁴−…) = 2επ(∫a²(…)(s+b²)… − ∫ds/(Δ(c²+s)) − …). Terms such as −∫ds/(Δ(c²+s)) lack the factor a²b²c². Riemann abandoned it and the final boxed-off formula is correct.
Scratch lines such as '4b⁴−a²b²+3b⁴+c²b² = b⁴' and '∫(sa²+b²)… − ∫(3b²+a²)… = ∫2s(a²−b²)' are fragmentary, not valid identities as written. They are side computations without consequence.

Otherwise every main step I checked is correct: the reality regimes, both kinetic coefficients, the p/q reduction, the σ coefficient, the final τ and ρ formulas, the c=∞ limit, and the c=a ⇒ ρ=0 case.

results.what: Stationary solution of the k=k'=0 (axes in a principal plane) Riemann equations: h,h',g,g' parametrised by τ,ρ, with existence only for 2c>a+b or 2c<a−b
results.modern_name: Riemann ellipsoids of types I–III (angular velocity and vorticity in a principal plane)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861; modern treatment by Chandrasekhar (Ellipsoidal Figures of Equilibrium, 1969)

results.what: Elimination of the pressure constant giving closed integral formulas for τ and ρ in terms of index-symbol-type integrals
results.modern_name: Equilibrium conditions of non-S-type Riemann ellipsoids in terms of the A_i, A_ij index symbols

results.what: Elliptic-cylinder limit c→∞ of the equilibrium formulas
results.modern_name: Limiting (infinite cylinder) case of Riemann ellipsoids
results.usually_credited_to: unsure; cylinder analogues treated later (e.g. Chandrasekhar and successors)

results.what: c=a forces ρ=0 in regime 1; boundary ρ=0 where the family joins rotation about a single axis
results.modern_name: Junction of type I/II/III Riemann ellipsoids with the S-type sequence
